subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual evals & next steps (Globex Retail)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kovacs <anna.kovacs@globexretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:02:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap: Multilingual evals & next steps

Hi Anna —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture next steps: 

Key takeaways:
- Primary goal: improve product QA and customer-facing summarization across EU markets (DE, FR, ES) and evaluate expansion to APAC (JP, KR).
- Current pain: inconsistent locale-specific responses, hallucination on legal/regulatory prompts, and throughput constraints during peak traffic.
- Success metrics: per-language F1/ROUGE targets for extraction tasks, human-rated fluency >= 4/5 for summaries, and median p95 generation latency < 300ms for short prompts.

Initial model recommendations (based on your usage profile and latency needs):
1) Redwood-4f-8k-quant (recommended pilot) — strong latency/cost balance for short conversational summaries; good EU language support in our benchmarks.
2) LLaMAx-13B-int8 (fallback) — better recall on long context; slightly higher latency but useful for heavy extraction flows.
3) Redwood-mt-lite (locale-tuned) — targeting higher fluency in German/French for product copy and legal phrasing.

Deliverables we’ll provide by next Tuesday (2027-04-06):
- Tailored benchmark report (attached CSV) with per-language scores for your sample prompt set.
- A starter multilingual prompt set (attached JSON) and recommended few-shot templates.
- Proposed pilot plan: 2-week canary in EU region w/ German & French, and parallel offline eval for JP/KR.

Questions we had for you to finalize scope:
- Can you share a 500–1,000-example sample for DE/FR (anonymized) we can use for evals?
- Any hard constraints on EU data residency or contractual terms?

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa (me): share benchmark CSV + prompt set (attached) and schedule 30-min follow-up to review results.
- Monica: run language-specific micro-evals and produce per-language error analysis.
- Rishi: prepare pricing estimate for the 2-week pilot and for Dedicated capacity option (if you want reserved throughput).

Proposed times for follow-up: Wed 2027-04-07 10:00-11:00 CEST or Thu 2027-04-08 14:00-15:00 CEST — what works for you?

Attachments:
- redwood_eval_benchmarks_v2.csv (initial per-language scores)
- multilingual-promptset-v3.json (starter prompts and templates)

Thanks again — excited to help validate model fit across your EU locales.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) Data residency: our EU customers require that any production inference for EU traffic be processed in-region. For the pilot, is it possible to run the canary entirely in eu-west-1?
2) APAC: We can provide a 600-example anonymized set for JP and KR, but those will be lower priority — is an offline eval sufficient to start?
3) Cost: rough order-of-magnitude for a 2-week pilot (EU canary + offline APAC eval) would help us get internal sign-off. Also curious about monitoring for regressions across locales — what does Redwood ship by default?

Also looping in my manager, Marco (cc’d in the product alias), who will want to review the benchmark approach.

If those answers look good, Wed 10:00 CEST works for the follow-up.

Thanks,
Anna

Marissa / Rishi —

I looked through the prompt set and the attached CSV. Proposed internal plan and quick tasking: 

Plan:
- Week 1: run zero-shot and few-shot evals across DE/FR/ES using Redwood-4f-8k-quant and Redwood-mt-lite. Generate per-prompt confusion matrices and human-fluency samples for spot checks.
- Week 1 (parallel): offline evaluation of JP/KR on the LLaMAx-13B-int8 to compare recall on longer extraction tasks.
- Week 2: run a small canary (5k requests/day) in eu-west-1 with prefix caching enabled and observe latency/cost. We'll capture token-level cost breakdowns.

Tasking:
- Monica: produce per-language error analysis and a short slide deck highlighting failure modes (legal phrasing, currency/unit localization, idiomatic phrasing).
- Rishi: draft pilot pricing (hosted pilot vs dedicated 1xA100 equivalent) and call out delta for in-region processing.
- Marissa: coordinate with Anna for the sample datasets and confirm follow-up slot.

Monitoring / regression guardrails:
- Baseline evals saved to the Drive folder. We'll run nightly automated checks comparing BLEU/ROUGE and a human-rated fluency rubric. Any >5% drop in key metric triggers alert to your team and ours.

I’ll start the runs today once we get the sample sets.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the quick reply and for confirming Wed 10:00 CEST — I’ll send the invite. Answers inline to your questions: 

1) EU in-region processing: yes — we can route the canary to eu-west-1 and ensure inference and token logs remain in-region for the duration of the pilot. We’ll provide a short addendum in the SOW to capture data residency guarantees.

2) APAC offline evals: offline evaluation is perfect to start. Monica will run the JP/KR runs and share a separate short report. If you want to move JP/KR to an in-region pilot later, we can schedule dedicated capacity in ap-northeast-1.

3) Cost estimate (rough):
- Hosted pilot (2 weeks, EU canary with 5k req/day): ~$7k–$10k, depends on model choice and avg tokens/req.
- Dedicated 1xA100 equivalent reserved for predictable throughput (monthly): pricing TBD in the formal quote but I’ll include a delta in Rishi’s estimate.

Monitoring / regressions: by default Redwood ships:
- nightly automated metric diffs (BLEU/ROUGE + custom rubric),
- per-request token-level traces + per-model latency percentiles,
- quality regression alerts that can be tied to your test prompt set and human review workflow.

Attached: smaller curated prompt subset (multilingual-promptset-v3-trimmed.json) to accelerate your anonymized data matching.

Action items before Wed 10:00 CEST:
- Anna: share anonymized DE/FR samples (500–1,000) and JP/KR 600-example set if available.
- Rishi: send pilot pricing and a brief note on Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.
- Monica: prepare per-language test plan and expected deliverables.

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4D-globex-evals
Benchmarks: https://app.redwood.ai/reports/DEAL-2027-452/benchmarks

Looking forward to the follow-up.

Best,
